evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.2: admīrābilis in dīcendō vir (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Worthy of admiration, of people, qualities and deeds. It also means “astonishing, strange” (Cicero’s word for the Stoic paradoxes), and it is often ironic: ō admīrābilem impudentiam! (Cic. Phil. 3.18).

terms.gloss: splendid, grand, impressive (of buildings, shows, preparations)
terms.comment: Of things, splendid and costly; of people, high-minded or fond of display, and in Plautus boastful (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: admirabilis · Lewis & Short: magnificus
